scopeDecisions.decision: The whole corpus is observed over REST v1; representative cases of every surface are also observed over gRPC google.firestore.v1. Client SDK paths (limitToLast reversal, listeners, caches) belong to FS-LISTEN-SDK.

The sandbox (default) database carries the lane superset conformance/fs-query-index.indexes.json (the shared conformance/firestore.indexes.json plus lane-only collection groups). The shared file stays unchanged because other campaigns bind its digest.

Under the strict profile a missing-index refusal matches production exactly, console link and encoded index included. The emulator profile keeps its firestore.indexes.json fragment hint and is not closure evidence.
Vector search (findNearest) on the Standard edition is in scope.
Pipeline execution semantics stay FS-ENTERPRISE-EXCLUDED; the Standard-edition refusal of ExecutePipeline is production behavior and is in scope.

Index and field administration methods (collectionGroups.indexes.*, collectionGroups.fields.*) that the API denominator assigns here belong to FS-CONFIG-LIFECYCLE; Listen target types (QueryTarget, BloomFilter, ExistenceFilter) belong to FS-LISTEN-SDK.
Read times on runQuery, runAggregationQuery and partitionQuery are observed here; queries inside transactions and transaction options stay in FS-TRANSACTION.

Closure evidence is the sandbox re-record. Historical production evidence (the 2026-09-07 matrix query rows, the aggregation corpora, the Explain v5 receipt and the 2026-09-08 index-merge check) corroborates it and stays immutable. The historical 324-row regression belongs to FS-DATA-WRITE, as do listDocuments, listCollectionIds and the index-entry write limits.

scopeDecisions.decision: Zero gap: response bodies, including error message text, must equal production after normalization. A documented divergence needs an owner decision naming the row.
Rules-based query authorization belongs to FS-RULES; this corpus runs with owner credentials.

conditions.note: EQUAL, NOT_EQUAL, ranges, ARRAY_CONTAINS, ARRAY_CONTAINS_ANY, IN and NOT_IN over every value class, including null, NaN, numeric int/double equivalence, type-restricted ranges, nested and quoted field paths and __name__ filters.
IS_NULL, IS_NOT_NULL, IS_NAN and IS_NOT_NAN on present, missing, nested and __name__ fields, with and without ordering.
AND and OR composites, nesting, single-child and duplicate filters, disjunctive expansion and result deduplication, ordered and limited disjunctions.
Refusals of malformed operators, values, field paths and __name__ values, and of forbidden filter combinations (negation, not-in, array-contains families, key equality with other inequalities).

Every query-plan limit as an accepted/refused pair one unit apart: 30 disjunctions (IN, ARRAY_CONTAINS_ANY, __name__ IN, OR and products), 10 NOT_IN values, 10 inequality fields, 100 components (root, subcollection, orders, disjunctions). The IN × IN and IN × ARRAY_CONTAINS_ANY product pairs (30/32, 30/33) cannot land on 31; the one-unit disjunction boundary is carried by the IN-29-or-one / IN-30-or-one and OR-30 / OR-31 pairs.
Default, explicit, multi-field, nested, map/array and cross-type ordering, missing-field exclusion, implied orders from inequalities, __name__ directions and order-clause refusals.
startAt/endAt with before true, false and omitted, prefixes, name tiebreaks, descending order, type-mismatched and empty cursors, __name__ reference validation and cursor refusals.
limit and offset values and wire forms, int32 bounds, negative values, skippedResults, offset past the end and the limitToLast wire form.
select with fields, nested leaves and maps, missing fields, empty lists, __name__, duplicates, invalid paths and unselected filter/order fields.
Collection and collection-group scopes from the root, existing, missing and absent parents, kindless queries, group-scoped filters and orders, __name__ ranges and cursors, and group counts.
count, sum and avg semantics over every numeric class and non-numeric values, upTo, limit/offset/cursor/order interplay, default and explicit aliases and every aggregation refusal.

findNearest with EUCLIDEAN, COSINE and DOT_PRODUCT, distance result fields and thresholds, the 1000 limit pair, malformed vectors and options, missing vector indexes, prefilters and other query clauses.
PartitionQuery on small and 2,000-document groups: partition counts, page size and tokens, range reconstruction, parents and every refusal.
Plan-only and analyzed Explain for queries, aggregations and findNearest over automatic, composite, merged and collection-group indexes, and Explain of refused queries.
Which queries automatic single-field indexes, composites, merges, collection-group scopes and exemptions serve, and the exact missing-index refusal (message and console link) when none does.

runQuery, runAggregationQuery and partitionQuery at a read time between writes, one microsecond before and one nanosecond after a commit, the one-hour retention boundary as a 59/61-minute pair (point-in-time recovery is disabled on the sandbox), and refusals of future, too-old and malformed read times.
REST request bodies and parents: empty, non-JSON and unknown fields, enum and integer encodings, from-clause collection ids including the 1500-byte pair, and collection or odd-depth parents.
ExecutePipeline on a Standard-edition database is refused over REST and gRPC; pipeline semantics themselves are FS-ENTERPRISE-EXCLUDED (scope decision Q4).
Representative queries, aggregations, refusals, Explain, findNearest, read times and partitions through google.firestore.v1 gRPC (scope decision Q1).
The whole corpus compared on one saved release artifact.
Independent clean-context closure and safety review of the final evidence.
